title: Warm blackberries on toast with kipper ricotta

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Kippers, ricotta, blackberries, honey, bread and watercress are all plain whole foods a grandparent could have had in.

supermarket.reason: Every item, including kipper fillets, ricotta and watercress, is an everyday Tesco line at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: Only a frying pan, a bowl and a toaster are needed, and the techniques are simple.

works.reason: Piling honey-sweetened, jammy blackberries straight onto smoked kipper ricotta is a jarring sweet and smoky-fish clash most families would not enjoy at breakfast, so it is unlikely to come out as a good dish.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes is enough to flake the kippers, zest the lemon, beat the ricotta and toast eight slices, and the eight minutes of cooking matches the 4-minute simmer plus 3 to 4 minutes for the berries.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: Early September is peak blackberry time, and the warm berries are the main topping rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Wholemeal toast with fish, ricotta, fruit and watercress makes a filling breakfast of real food, with only a spoon of honey added.
